To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a) the combination of a state-of-the- art classifier with a state-of-theart feature set yields a state-of-the -art detector, b) the combination of multiple feature channels yields a better detector than any single channel, c) the combination of different feature channels yields a significantly better detector than the combination of the same feature channels with different weights, and d) a simple linear combination of kernels is sufficient to obtain the best detector

multiple kernel learning can be used to learn an optimal linear combination of kernels, each of them capturing a specific feature channel; and that this combination of kernels can be used to train an object detector that is more accurate than a detector based on a single feature channel.

1) multiple kernels are a powerful tool for object category detection, 2) a state-of-the- art image classifier is a powerful tool for searching for an object in an image, and 3) a state-of- the-art object category detector is a powerful tool to learn an object category model.
In summary, our research is concerned with
two questions: How to design an object detector? And how to learn a combination of object detectors?

(1) the use of a state-of-theart image classifier as an object detector (2) the use of multiple kernel learning for combining features and kernels (3) the use of the distribution of edges as an image feature.

(a) the design of a novel feature space, (b) a multiple kernel approach to learn an optimal feature combination for object detection, and (c) the evaluation of our approach on a challenging dataset of 8 object categories.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed method is able to achieve state-of-the-art performance on the PASCAL VOC 2007 object category detection task.
the combination of multiple features, multiple scales and multiple kernels leads to a significant improvement in object category detection.
our system achieves the best results to date on the challenging PASCAL VOC 2008 dataset.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have achieved a 10.5% absolute improvement over the state-of-the-art in object detection.
we have achieved a 10% relative improvement in the mean Average Precision (mAP) over the state-of-the-art on PASCAL VOC2007, and a 6% improvement on VOC2006.
we have developed a novel framework for object detection that is competitive with the current state of the art.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the optimal kernel for a given object category is highly dependent on the feature set and the classifier.
the optimal combination of features is very different from the individual performance of each of the feature channels.
it is possible to obtain a stateof-the art category detector without any handcrafted features or object-specific training data.
